sents.t: In America, almost everyone talks about their “credit score.” It’s a number that shows banks if you pay your bills on time.
You often need good credit to rent an apartment, get a loan for a car, or even get some phone plans.
Last winter, I didn’t have a credit score at all, because I had never had a credit card.
Danny works at a bank, so I asked him for advice.
“You should start with a simple card with a low limit,” he said.
“Use it for small things, like gas or groceries, and pay the whole bill every month. Never pay late, and never spend more than you have.”
I applied online, and the bank approved me with a limit of five hundred dollars.
“That’s why you have to pay off everything every month. If you don’t, your debt will grow very fast.”
Since then, I have used my card only for gas, and I have paid it off every month.
This week, I checked my credit score for the first time: 710!
